three_distinct_mechanisms.mechanism: Nuxt module addComponentsDir (directory scan, auto-registered, no import needed)
evidence: packages/modules/narduk-core/src/module.ts:544-547 addComponentsDir({path: '../runtime/app/components', pathPrefix: false}), gated behind options.app (module.ts:539)
packages/modules/narduk-seo/src/module.ts:371-378 TWO addComponentsDir calls: '../app/components' and '../components' (the second is the OgImage/*.takumi.vue family)
three_distinct_mechanisms.notes: pathPrefix:false means components register under their bare filename regardless of subfolder (app/, shared/, admin/, auth/) -- e.g. shared/AppEmptyState.vue is just <AppEmptyState>, not <SharedAppEmptyState>. A name collision between two modules' components dirs would silently shadow one (last-registered wins); not observed today but relevant if a new 'table' family lands inside an existing module.

three_distinct_mechanisms.mechanism: Nuxt module addComponent (single-component registration, auto-registered, gated by an options flag)
evidence: packages/modules/narduk-mapkit-nuxt/src/module.ts:62-70 addComponent() called twice (AppMapKit, AppMapKitCallout) inside `if (options.component)`, options.component defaults true (module.ts:45)
three_distinct_mechanisms.notes: Same auto-registration outcome as addComponentsDir but declared per-component and independently toggleable.

three_distinct_mechanisms.mechanism: Plain Vue package, no Nuxt module at all -- consumer must explicitly import, nothing is auto-registered
evidence: packages/design/narduk-ui/package.json has no 'nuxt' entry and no module.ts anywhere in the package; exports map ('./instruments', './instruments/*.vue') resolves straight to source .vue files (package.json exports block)
packages/design/narduk-ui/README.md:15-16 'Source is TypeScript, Vue, and CSS with no build step -- consumers import the exported paths directly. Pin an exact version.'
packages/design/narduk-charts has no module.ts under src/; package.json peerDependencies is only {vue: '^3.3.0'} (package.json:66-68), no nuxt peer
packages/design/narduk-charts/README.md:114 'import { NardukLineChart } from ...' -- explicit import required in every consuming .vue file
three_distinct_mechanisms.notes: narduk-charts DOES have a real build (vite lib mode, 6 entry points: main/line/bar/pie/candle/studies, package.json:50-51,9-41) producing dist/*.js + dist/narduk-charts.css. narduk-ui ships raw .vue SFCs with zero bundling (package.json 'build' script is only 'vue-tsc --noEmit', package.json script block).

2_registration_mechanics.what_a_new_shared_family_needs_for_auto_: Cheapest path: land the new .vue files inside an existing Nuxt module's already-scanned components dir (e.g. narduk-core's runtime/app/components/shared/) -- zero new wiring, but couples the new family's release cadence to that module's. Clean-ownership path: give it its own Nuxt module with addComponentsDir/addComponent like narduk-mapkit-nuxt -- a new package, a module.ts, and (per section 9/10) a create-narduk-app manifest.ts pin to actually reach new apps. Either path yields real Nuxt auto-registration. The narduk-ui/narduk-charts path (plain package, manual import) is the cheapest to publish but is NOT auto-registered and -- per section 10 -- is not even wired into create-narduk-app's scaffold today, so it stays invisible to new apps unless a human remembers to add + import it.

3_styling_contract.two_parallel_systems_is_a_real_confirmed: packages/modules/narduk-auth/tests/auth-login-card-contrast.test.ts:1-36 is a real production regression (operator-portal#238): AuthLoginCard.vue used Nuxt UI's `text-muted`, which resolves against Nuxt UI's --ui-bg and broke (4.17:1, under the 4.5:1 AA floor) when operator-portal repointed --ui-bg to a custom ground color. The test's own comment states verbatim: 'packages/design/narduk-ui/tokens.css ... is an unrelated token set consumed via .ns-* classes by the five status apps ... not by Nuxt UI's semantic colour scale that AuthLoginCard.vue actually uses' (lines 27-31). This is the codebase confirming, from a real incident, that a new shared component (a table) must pick ONE of these two systems and that picking wrong has already broken production once.

4_narduk_shell_proposal.status: proposed, not built (docs/proposals/narduk-shell.md:3); filed as narduk-libs#119
4_narduk_shell_proposal.summary: A new package @narduk-enterprises/narduk-shell would supply a sectioned, always-expanded (never icon-only, never collapsible-tree) left-nav app shell plus a generalized PACC-TRAC-derived token layer (--pt-* -> structural surfaces/ink/radius/shadow/type, brand-configurable accent+structure pair), as a Nuxt module the same shape as narduk-core. API sketch: modules:['@narduk-enterprises/narduk-shell'], nardukShell:{accent, structure, sections:[{id, label, items:[{label, to, badge?}]}]}, then <NardukShell><slot/></NardukShell> in the app's default layout, plus useNardukShellSections() for runtime mutation. Explicitly composes Nuxt UI (not a fork), explicitly NOT the Status Design System's replacement, explicitly layout-only (no auth-gating, no data-fetching). Target adopters: operator-portal (first), been-sober-for, borderwaitstat-us, gonogo, and eventually create-narduk-app's default module list -- explicitly NOT the five status-family apps. Sizing note: filed as an issue rather than built because the section-rail interaction needs a design pass with Logan first (docs/proposals/narduk-shell.md:142-150).
4_narduk_shell_proposal.relevance_to_table_work: No table/list-page primitives in scope here at all -- this proposal is chrome/nav/tokens only, so it doesn't compete with or substitute for a shared table component, but a table component family would likely want to live in the same 'app shell' tier of package once narduk-shell exists.

6_server_list_helpers.conclusion: THREE list endpoints inside narduk-libs itself, THREE different shapes (full page/limit/total envelope; ad hoc unreadOnly+limit; no params, hardcoded cap, raw array). No shared parseListQuery()/buildListResponse() helper exists anywhere in narduk-core or narduk-auth server utils -- confirmed by grep across both packages' server trees for paginat/parsePagination/listQuery, zero hits.

eslint_rule_require_limit_on_drizzle_lis.what_it_enforces: Flags every Drizzle list query -- both db.select().from(...) builder chains and db.query.X.findMany() relational-API calls, including through single-assignment destructuring/aliasing -- that is not bounded by an explicit non-undefined .limit()/limit option, UNLESS it is filtered to a single row by primary key (findFirst, .where(eq(pk, id))) or is an aggregate (count()/groupBy()). No autofix by design (comment: 'the right bound is a product decision'). Directly relevant to any shared server-side list helper: the helper must still force each call site to pass a real limit value to stay lint-clean.

narduk_testkit_ui_quality_analyzer.what_it_checks: NOT a component-behavior or accessibility checker. ui-quality.ts is a Playwright screenshot capture harness (captureNamedLocator/captureFullPageAudit, writes a manifest.json of route/element screenshots). ui-quality-analyzer.ts then walks those screenshots with `sharp` and computes per-image mean brightness + per-channel stdev (to catch near-blank/broken captures), file size and dimensions, and checks the actual screenshot/full-page counts against a manifest-declared minimum -- producing a score/warnings/failures summary. It proves visual-QA coverage was taken and isn't blank; it does not assert a table sorts correctly or paginates correctly.

accessibility_helpers.what_it_provides: axe-core WCAG 2.2 AA baseline assertions (assertAgainstAccessibilityBaseline, WCAG_2_2_AA_TAGS), text-zoom overflow checks (expectNoOverflowAtTextZoom), color-alone-state checks (expectStateNotCarriedByColourAlone -- directly relevant to a sortable-column/status-badge table), reduced-motion checks. This is real, reusable infra a new table component's e2e suite could adopt.

journeys_package.what_it_is: Declarative demo/journey-to-test-and-video compiler (defineCatalog -> tests + screenshots + walkthrough video). General demo-flow tooling, not component-unit-test infra; spec lives in agent-infrastructure per its README.

8_design_system_build.mechanics: packages/design/design-system-build/app/app.vue (128 lines) is a SINGLE hand-authored Nuxt page. Each gallery card is a <section class="preview-card" data-design-card="..." data-name="..." data-group="..."> block the author writes by hand, importing the real component and supplying fixed demonstration props/fixtures. `pnpm design-system:build` prerenders this page and extracts each card's static HTML + compiled CSS into dist/design-system/, with a build-manifest.json recording package versions/hashes/coverage. There is NO automatic discovery of components -- nothing scans packages/design or packages/modules for .vue files.

8_design_system_build.what_a_new_component_needs: A human must hand-write a new <section data-design-card=... data-group=...> block in this one app.vue file, importing the component and inventing demonstration fixture props. No manifest entry, config file, or convention triggers auto-inclusion.

changesets.detail: baseBranch main, access restricted (GitHub Packages, per narduk-ui/package.json publishConfig), updateInternalDependencies patch, no fixed/linked groups (every package versions independently).

quality_gate.detail: `pnpm run quality` = versions:check (scripts/sync-generator-package-versions.mjs --check) && release-plan:check (scripts/check-generator-release-plan.mjs) && quality:artifacts (format:check && lint && typecheck && build && test), each running via turbo across every packages/*/* workspace.

publish_gate.detail: Two-job pipeline: (1) verify-ci job runs scripts/verify-release-ci.mjs to require the exact current main SHA already has a fully-green required-CI run before anything publishes; (2) the release job checks out that exact verified SHA, runs changesets (release:version / release:publish via scripts/publish-verified-packages.mjs), then scripts/verify-published-packages.mjs to confirm immutable published versions actually landed on the registry.

consumer_fixture_requirement.detail: 'New package releases must be installable from their packed artifact by a consumer fixture outside the workspace.' -- i.e. pnpm pack --dry-run plus an out-of-workspace install-and-import smoke test is required validation before publishing (release:consumer-smoke script), not just an in-repo build.

9_release_mechanics.cost_of_adding_a_package_or_subpath_expo: scripts/check-generator-release-plan.mjs (part of release-plan:check, part of `quality`) reads create-narduk-app's src/manifest.ts for every '@narduk-enterprises/*' version it pins (check-generator-release-plan.mjs:26-31), then fails CI if any pinned package has uncommitted changes without a matching changeset (so the generator's pin and the real package version can't silently drift). Concretely: adding a genuinely NEW package (a 'components' family) means: a new packages/<family>/<name> directory wired into pnpm-workspace.yaml, its own package.json (build/lint/typecheck/test:unit scripts, publishConfig, exports map), a changeset, passing the full quality gate above including an out-of-workspace consumer-fixture install, AND -- only if it should reach new scaffolds -- a create-narduk-app manifest.ts pin plus a generate.ts wiring change (see section 10). None of this is hard, but it is real per-package ceremony, and today's evidence (narduk-ui, narduk-charts) shows a package can be fully published and versioned for a long time while still never reaching create-narduk-app's scaffold.

never_wired.evidence: Neither name appears anywhere in create-narduk-app/src/manifest.ts's PACKAGE_VERSIONS map (manifest.ts:6-17) or anywhere else in create-narduk-app/src/*.ts (grep for both names across the package, zero hits outside this audit). A freshly scaffolded app gets zero narduk-ui instruments and zero narduk-charts, opt-in or otherwise.

scaffolded_ui_surface.detail: apps/web/app/app.vue (generate.ts:423-431) is just <UApp><NuxtLayout><NuxtPage /></NuxtLayout></UApp>. apps/web/app/pages/index.vue (generate.ts:435+) is SEO-fixture boilerplate (useSeo/useWebPageSchema), no table/list scaffold, no sample data page. There is nothing in a fresh scaffold that any list/table pattern could extend -- it is a blank slate.

10_generator_create_narduk_app.eslint_capability_packs_gap_surprise_fin: generate.ts:528 hardcodes the generated apps/web/eslint.config.mjs to capabilityPacks: ['core', 'correctness', 'complexity', 'formatting'] and the generated root eslint.config.mjs (generate.ts ~533-538) to composeSharedConfigs('core', 'correctness', 'complexity', 'formatting') -- NEITHER includes 'design-system' NOR 'nuxt-ui', despite eslint-config's own defaultCapabilityPresetOrder listing both as defaults (packages/tooling/eslint-config/eslint-app-config.mjs:411-418). This is the only occurrence of capabilityPacks in create-narduk-app's source (grep confirms). Net effect: a brand-new scaffolded app does NOT get the <table>-is-banned / raw-Tailwind-color-is-banned guardrails from section 3 unless a human manually adds 'design-system' to its eslint config after generation -- the estate's own generator ships apps in a state its own lint-config package's defaults consider incomplete.

tx_spends_data_table_card.wires: <UTable :sorting :sorting-options="{manualSorting:true}" @update:sorting> (server-driven sort only, NOT client TanStack sorting), <UPagination v-model:page> computed from meta.offset/meta.limit (classic offset pagination, not cursor), USkeleton, UCard, local EmptyState (its own #components auto-import, NOT narduk-libs's AppEmptyState)
tx_spends_data_table_card.mobile_strategy: Renders BOTH a card-list (<article> per row, class md:hidden) and the <UTable> (class hidden md:block) simultaneously and toggles visibility with Tailwind breakpoints -- not one adaptive layout, two full DOM trees.
tx_spends_data_table_card.loading_ux: Sophisticated: keeps last-stable-rows visible at reduced opacity while a new page loads, falls back to 10 skeleton placeholder rows only on true first load, computes a min-height from row count to prevent scroll/layout jump during the transition.
gaps_a_shared_component_should_close: No column-type system at all: every cell (badges, row-links, currency formatting) is hand-authored per page via named slots (#${key}-data) -- confirmed by reading apps/web/app/pages/transactions/index.vue:226-293, which reimplements UBadge/UButton-link/currency-format cells from scratch
No client-side sort/paginate mode -- manualSorting:true is baked in, so any app without a server-paginated endpoint can't use this component as-is
No search/filter bar integration -- composed ad hoc by each page outside the component
isAmountColumnKey() right-alignment is a hardcoded column-name heuristic (key==='amount'||endsWith('_amount')...), not a declared column type

Carries a 'narduk/file-size-budget' eslint-disable at line 1 -- already over whatever budget an estate max-lines rule sets (packages/tooling/eslint-config/configs/template.mjs:7,58 confirms this rule exists in narduk-libs's own eslint-config as the 'Replaces narduk/file-size-budget' core max-lines rule) -- i.e. even this app's own team already flagged the component as too big.
